name: BUILD A BEAR WORKSHOP

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter, which is now the LONG case, is that I am extrapolating one seasonally small quarter into a five-year decay rate. Q2 is Build-A-Bear's weakest quarter; the holiday quarter carries the year's margin, and a 340 basis point gross-margin decline driven partly by occupancy deleverage reverses mechanically if revenue stabilises, because the rent does not go up. The company still guides to $60-68M of pre-tax income on $500-525M — an 11.8-13.0% pre-tax margin — which is four to five times the fiscal 2019 structure and is being delivered while the top line falls, which is evidence of resilience rather than collapse. The stock is at $30.11 with a 10.8% FCFF yield, roughly 9x enterprise value to free cash flow, and management has been buying back stock steadily. If free cash flow merely holds at $38M, the equity is worth far more than $30. At -8% I am pricing a permanent, compounding reversal from a single quarter's promotional intensity.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Q3 and Q4 fiscal 2026 gross margin against the 54.2% just posted and against the prior year. If gross margin recovers toward 57-58% in the holiday quarter and the full year lands inside the $60-68M pre-tax guide, the Q2 compression was seasonal and promotional rather than structural, and -8% is too harsh. If gross margin stays down 300+ basis points through the holiday quarter and the pre-tax guide is cut a third time, the reversion is confirmed and even -8% will prove generous.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The evidence is now genuinely split, which is why I moved partway rather than all the way. Against me: the full-year pre-tax guide of $60-68M still implies a margin structure nothing like 2019, and there is no evidence of balance-sheet stress. For me: two guidance cuts in one fiscal year, a 340 basis point gross-margin decline with a named cause, pre-tax income down 24.1% on a 7.2% revenue decline (2.4x operating deleverage), and a Chief Growth Officer terminated the day before the cut — which is a board that has concluded the growth plan is not working, not a board managing a seasonal blip.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The decomposition I could not do this morning and still cannot do: how much of the post-2020 margin step is structural mix shift — franchise and partner-operated royalties, 37 countries versus 19, less direct mall exposure — versus a pricing and collectibles cycle. That needs the segment detail in the 10-K, and SEC egress is blocked from this runtime. It is the whole question, and my -8% is a judgement between two poles rather than an answer to it. I also could not obtain prior-year Q2 gross margin in absolute terms, only the 340 basis point change management reported.

what_changed: Two items that were open this morning are now closed, and both go against the long case. (1) The item 5.02 buried in the 2026-08-27 8-K alongside the guidance cut is the termination of David Henderson as Chief Growth Officer, effective 2026-08-26 — an officer dismissed the day before the second guidance cut of the fiscal year, with a separation and release agreement. (2) The Q2 fiscal 2026 margin detail: revenue $115.3M, down 7.2%; pre-tax income $11.6M against $15.3M in the prior-year quarter, down 24.1%; GROSS MARGIN 54.2%, down 340 basis points year over year, attributed to occupancy cost deleverage and increased promotional activity. Full-year revenue guidance cut to $500-525M from $530-550M. The share price is $30.11 against $29.85 at this morning's screen.
consensus_case: The market prices -11.8% annual FCFF decay for five years, and after today's research I think that is arithmetic rather than pessimism. Build-A-Bear's current earnings power is unprecedented in its own history: in fiscal 2018 the company lost $18.5M pre-tax, in fiscal 2019 it made $1.6M of pre-tax income on $338.5M of revenue, and it now guides to $60-68M of pre-tax income on $500-525M. That step happened during the 2021-2024 collectibles-and-pricing boom and has held for three flat years at roughly $38M of free cash flow. The bear case is simply that the step was a cycle. What the market is watching is that the cycle has turned: fiscal 2026 revenue guidance has now been cut twice in one year, to $500-525M from $530-550M, on 'summer trend products' underperforming — a product-cycle explanation, which is what reversion looks like at the start. Reverting $38M of FCFF toward the low $20Ms over five years is exactly what -11.8% a year produces, and that is a defensible read of a discretionary mall retailer whose product cycle has visibly rolled over.
base_case_rationale: I underwrite roughly -8% five-year FCFF growth, cut from the -4% I carried this morning, and the cut is the whole point of today's pass. This morning's write-up asserted that pre-tax margin was 'still roughly 12.5%, nowhere near the pre-2020 structure' and concluded that 'the first crack is in the top line, not yet in the economics.' That assertion is wrong, and I found it wrong by looking for the evidence my own devil's advocate had nominated. Q2 pre-tax margin was 10.1% ($11.6M on $115.3M) against 12.3% ($15.3M on $124.2M) a year earlier, and gross margin fell 340 basis points to 54.2% on occupancy deleverage and promotional activity. Occupancy deleverage is the mechanism that turns a mid-single-digit revenue decline into a double-digit profit decline in mall retail: the rent is fixed, so every point of lost comparable revenue drops through. Promotional activity is the mechanism that says the pricing power which created the 2021-2024 step is being given back. Those are not top-line cracks, they are the economics, and they are visible now. I still do not think the business reverts all the way to its 2019 structure — the international, franchise and partner-operated mix is genuinely larger and genuinely capital-light, and that is real — so I do not go all the way to the market's -11.8%. But -4% was a number formed before I had the margin data, and holding it today would be theatre.
key_risks: Post-2020 margins may be a cycle rather than a structure — the question I could not close this morning and still cannot
Gross margin fell 340 basis points in Q2 on occupancy deleverage and promotional activity; both are structural mechanisms in mall retail, not one-offs
Two guidance cuts in one fiscal year, with pre-tax income down 24.1% on a 7.2% revenue decline
A Chief Growth Officer terminated the day before the second cut
Tariff exposure on Asian-sourced plush, and the fiscal 2026 Q1 result was flattered by roughly $7M of prior-year tariff refunds
$16.5M average daily dollar volume on a $377M company
watch_for: Q3 and Q4 fiscal 2026 gross margin against the 54.2% just posted — recovery toward 57-58% hands it back to the long case
Whether the $60-68M fiscal 2026 pre-tax guide is cut a third time
Net new unit count and the franchise/partner mix — the capital-light half of the structural argument
Who, if anyone, replaces the Chief Growth Officer, and whether the growth plan is restated
